findings.reason: Step 1.1 identifies the product of two complex shifted-QR factors with the real positive-diagonal factor up to signs, but the individual shifted factorizations have no stated phase convention. QR uniqueness gives diagonal unit-modulus phases in general. Repair the proof by using those phases to transfer the unreduced Hessenberg property, then align the real first columns using p(H)e1 = Q_e R_e e1 before applying the real implicit-Q lemma. The relevant full treatment discusses the real orthogonal implicit-Q comparison and Francis polynomial step in the [Cornell lecture](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs6210/2025fa/lec/2025-10-29.html).

The Definition promises an accumulated backward-error bound but gives only per-update coefficients and a general outward-evaluation clause. Specify a finite accumulation rule covering Hessenberg initialization, every chase update, and deflation writes, plus an inconclusive branch when no rigorous bound can be evaluated. A conservative rho/beta recurrence can keep the work linear in the number of updates after an O(n^2) initialization.

The proof establishes the perturbation bound formula, but does not connect it to the algorithm's promised returned certificate. After the algorithm defines its accumulator, show that its returned value rigorously upper-bounds the theorem's sum.

The current complexity proof does not count work for producing the backward-error certificate. With an O(1)-per-update recurrence and O(n^2) initialization, the stated asymptotic bound remains valid, but the proof needs an owner-side accounting update.
